data.title: Top Nav
data.tagline: Place the main navigation across the top of the page
data.description: A top-navigation layout works when a product has a small number of primary sections and needs wide content space below. Keep labels short, show the current section, and decide how the navigation collapses on narrow screens.

use: Product with a few main sections
Content that needs full page width
avoid: Squeeze many deep sections into one row
Let navigation wrap into an accidental second line
Copy the desktop row unchanged onto a phone

lessonPractice.title: A content site has five top-level destinations—Home, Articles, Topics, About, and Search—with no deep hierarchy. Which page structure is direct?

options.label: Use a top-navigation layout, constrain reading width, and collect secondary entries on mobile
options.feedback: A small set of primary destinations fits persistent top access while leaving the main content clear and wide.

options.label: Use a wide permanent sidebar for the five entries and leave the remaining width to articles
options.feedback: Sidebars fit deeper or tool-oriented navigation; these few entries would consume reading width without adding clarity.

options.label: Remove page navigation and append Articles, Topics, and About into one long homepage
options.feedback: These serve different content tasks, and merging them weakens distinct URLs, search, and return paths.

data.agentPrompt: Use a top-navigation layout for the content site: put brand, five primary destinations, and search in the top bar, constrain article width, and collect secondary entries on mobile. Verify current-page state, long titles, and sticky offset.
